nodes.label: [G01] Solar PV Cyber-Physical System (CPS) Disruption: Compromise inverter operations to disrupt grid stability, damage equipment, or halt power generation

children.label: [H01] Spoofing Attacks: Manipulate control signals or identities to deceive CPS components
[H02] Protocol Spoofing: Exploit weak authentication in Modbus/DNP3/OPC UA to inject falsified commands
[V01] Modbus/DNP3 Lack of Authentication: Default configurations allow unauthenticated command injection
[A01] Inverter Control Interface: Modbus/TCP port 502 exposed to spoofed setpoint injections (e.g., voltage/frequency adjustments)
[U01] Attacker
[A02] Gateway DNP3 Stack: Vulnerable to unauthenticated control messages from spoofed master stations
[U01] Attacker
[H03] Firmware Update Spoofing: Compromise update mechanisms to deploy malicious firmware
[V02] Unsecured Over-the-Air (OTA) Updates: Lack of code-signing verification in inverter firmware update process
[A03] Inverter OTA Update Port: HTTP/HTTPS endpoint (e.g., port 80/443) accepting unsigned firmware binaries
[U01] Attacker
[A04] Cloud Update Server: Compromised or spoofed server pushing backdoored firmware via MQTT/REST APIs
[U01] Attacker
[H04] HMI Session Spoofing: Hijack operator sessions to issue unauthorized commands
[V03] Weak Session Management: Predictable session tokens or missing CSRF protections in HMI web interface
[A05] HMI Web Portal: Port 80/443 with cookie-based auth vulnerable to session replay
[U01] Attacker
[H05] Tampering Attacks: Unauthorized modification of hardware, software, or data
[H06] Physical Tampering: Direct manipulation of inverter hardware or local interfaces
[V04] Unsecured Local Ports: USB/serial/Ethernet ports with no authentication or logging
[A06] Inverter USB Configuration Port: Exposed port allowing firmware flashes or debug access
[U01] Attacker
[A07] PLC Serial Port: RS-232/485 interface with default credentials for programming
[U01] Attacker
[V05] Safety Bypass Vulnerabilities: Jumpers or debug headers allowing disabling of protective relays
[A08] Inverter PCB: Exposed test points or jumpers to disable overvoltage/overcurrent protection
[U01] Attacker
[H07] Communication Tampering: Intercept and modify in-transit data between components
[V06] Unencrypted Fieldbus Traffic: Modbus RTU/Profibus messages susceptible to MITM modifications
[A09] Modbus RTU Bus: Shared serial bus between inverter and sensors/actuators (e.g., RS-485)
[U01] Attacker
[V07] Rogue Gateway Injection: Compromised protocol translator (e.g., Modbus-to-MQTT) altering telemetry/commands
[A10] Protocol Gateway Device: Linux/RTOS-based translator with weak access controls
[U01] Attacker
[H08] Data Integrity Tampering: Alter stored configurations or telemetry to induce unsafe operations
[V08] Unprotected Configuration Files: Plaintext or weakly encrypted inverter settings (e.g., MPPT curves, grid codes)
[A11] Inverter Configuration File: Stored on local flash or SD card with no integrity checks
[U01] Attacker
[V09] False Telemetry Injection: Compromised sensors feeding manipulated data to control loops
[A12] Temperature Sensor: I2C/analog sensor feeding falsified overheating data to trigger shutdowns
[U01] Attacker
[H10] Repudiation Attacks: Obscure attack origins by exploiting weak logging or audit trails
[V10] Missing or Tamperable Logs: Inverter/PLC event logs disabled, overwritable, or stored in plaintext
[A13] Inverter Event Log: Local circular buffer with no cryptographic protections
[U01] Attacker
[A14] PLC Audit Trail: Syslog/SEL events sent unencrypted to HMI, susceptible to interception/modification
[U01] Attacker
[V11] Anonymous Control Actions: Commands executed without operator attribution (e.g., Modbus function codes)
[A15] Modbus Write Coils (FC5): Unattributed command to toggle inverter relays/breakers
[U01] Attacker
[H12] Information Disclosure: Exfiltrate sensitive data to enable further attacks
[V12] Unencrypted Communication Channels: Cleartext protocols leaking telemetry or credentials
[A16] Modbus/TCP Cleartext: Port 502 traffic exposing inverter registers (e.g., power output, faults)
[U01] Attacker
[A17] Anonymous MQTT Broker: Telemetry published to unsecured MQTT topics (e.g., 'solar/inverter/#')
[U01] Attacker
[V13] Hardcoded Credentials: Default or backdoor credentials in firmware/HMI
[A18] Inverter Default Credentials: 'admin:admin' or vendor-specific backdoors in web interface
[U01] Attacker
[A19] PLC Engineering Credentials: Hardcoded 'service' account for vendor diagnostics
[U01] Attacker
[V14] Firmware Reverse Engineering: Extractable firmware binaries containing proprietary algorithms or crypto keys
[A20] Inverter Firmware Binary: Downgradable or dumpable via JTAG/UART with weak readout protection
[U01] Attacker
[H15] Denial-of-Service (DoS) Attacks: Disrupt inverter operations or communications
[V15] Network Flooding: Vulnerability to packet storms on fieldbus or IP networks
[A21] Modbus/UDP Flood: Port 502 UDP flood causing inverter communication timeout
[U01] Attacker
[A22] HMI Web Interface: Slowloris-style attack on port 80/443 exhausting connections
[U01] Attacker
[V16] Firmware Crash Triggers: Malformed packets or commands causing inverter reboot/lockup
[A23] Modbus Fuzzing: Crafted Modbus PDUs triggering buffer overflows in inverter stack
[U01] Attacker
[A24] Malformed DNP3 Objects: Invalid object headers causing PLC parse errors
[U01] Attacker
[V17] Physical DoS: Overload or damage inverter components via control commands
[A25] Actuator Overload: Rapid PWM cycling or relay toggling causing thermal stress
[U01] Attacker
[A26] Grid Desynchronization: Spoofed grid frequency commands forcing inverter trip
[U01] Attacker
[H18] Elevation of Privilege: Gain unauthorized high-level access to inverter controls
[V18] Privilege Escalation: Exploit vulnerabilities to move from low to high privileges
[V19] HMI Remote Code Execution: Buffer overflow in HMI web server (e.g., CVE-202X-1234)
[A27] HMI Web Server: Apache/Boa server with stack overflow in CGI handler
[U01] Attacker
[V20] PLC Ladder Logic Injection: Unauthorized modifications to control logic via engineering port
[A28] PLC Programming Port: Ethernet port with weak auth for ladder logic uploads
[U01] Attacker
[V21] Credential Theft: Extract or reuse credentials to access high-privilege functions
[A29] HMI Password Database: Plaintext or weakly hashed credentials in HMI config files
[U01] Attacker
[A30] Engineering Workstation: Stored inverter/PLC credentials in vendor software (e.g., Siemens TIA Portal)
[U01] Attacker
[H22] Lateral Movement: Pivot from compromised components to target the inverter
[V22] Compromised Adjacent Systems: Exploit trust relationships with EMS/SCADA or peer inverters
[A31] EMS/SCADA Trusted Link: Modbus/OPC UA connection from compromised SCADA to inverter
[U01] Attacker
[A32] Peer Inverter: SunSpec/IEC 61850 trust relationship allowing lateral command injection
[U01] Attacker
[V23] Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious components or updates from third-party vendors
[A33] Third-Party Firmware: Compromised inverter firmware from OEM or integrator
[U01] Attacker
[A34] Vendor Diagnostic Tools: Backdoored engineering software (e.g., SolarEdge SetApp)
